transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is that... I just don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. 

It's just flat. Even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or, you know, if something at work goes really well... I just can't seem to feel good about it. I just don't feel much of anything good right now.
How long have you been feeling this way—unable to feel happiness or closeness—has it been days, weeks, or longer?
It's been a lot longer than a few weeks. It's, uh, it's actually been going on since the retrofit accident. That was about a year and seven months ago now. Ever since then, it's just been like this.
Since the accident, have you experienced any intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about it, or found yourself avoiding things that remind you of it?

Yeah, I have. It doesn't even take much to set it off. Just hearing a normal alarm at the plant, or... or seeing a retrofit checklist on a clipboard. Even just the smell of hot metal. It's like I'm right back there. I can see him lying on the floor, and I hear everyone yelling for help all over again. It just hits me out of nowhere.
Besides feeling emotionally flat, have you also been feeling persistently sad, down, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I don't... I don't feel sad or hopeless, exactly. It's not like I'm walking around crying or feeling down all day. It's really just what I mentioned before—just flat. It's more of a blank feeling than a sad one, if that makes sense.
